title: Influence, Advocacy, Political Finance and Intelligence Organizations
scope: Public-source organizational research. This layer maps what organizations are, how they are funded or governed, what they publicly do, and how they connect to institutions. It does not infer secret control or misconduct from association alone.

records.name: American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU)
records.definition: A U.S. nonprofit civil-liberties organization that litigates, advocates and conducts public education around constitutional rights and civil liberties.

records.name: Anti-Defamation League (ADL)
records.definition: A U.S.-based nonprofit organization focused on antisemitism, extremism, civil rights and related education and advocacy. Its research publications are frequently used as secondary-source evidence in extremist-movement mapping.
research_dimensions: relationships with government and civil society

records.name: Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC)
records.definition: A U.S. nonprofit civil-rights organization that conducts litigation, advocacy and research including public monitoring of extremist organizations.

records.name: Human Rights Watch
records.definition: An international nongovernmental organization that investigates and reports on human-rights conditions and advocates for policy responses.

records.name: Amnesty International
records.definition: A global human-rights movement that conducts research, campaigns and advocacy concerning human-rights violations.

records.name: Open Society Foundations
records.definition: A philanthropic network that funds civil-society, justice, governance, health and rights initiatives in multiple countries.

records.name: Planned Parenthood Action Fund
records.definition: The advocacy and electoral political arm associated with Planned Parenthood's broader movement, distinct from the charitable and healthcare entities that operate under related branding.

records.name: NRA Institute for Legislative Action (NRA-ILA)
records.definition: The National Rifle Association's legislative advocacy arm, focused on firearms-policy advocacy and political engagement.
mechanisms: scorecards and endorsements through the broader NRA political ecosystem

records.name: Future Forward USA
records.definition: A U.S. independent-expenditure political committee that has operated as a major Democratic-aligned electoral spending vehicle.

records.name: Senate Leadership Fund
records.definition: A Republican-aligned independent-expenditure-only committee focused on Senate elections.

records.name: Congressional Leadership Fund
records.definition: A Republican-aligned independent-expenditure committee focused primarily on U.S. House elections.

records.name: Club for Growth Action
records.definition: An independent-expenditure political committee associated with the Club for Growth policy network and conservative electoral advocacy.

records.name: EMILY's List
records.definition: A U.S. political organization that supports Democratic women candidates who favor abortion rights, through fundraising, endorsements, training and electoral advocacy.

records.name: America PAC
records.definition: A U.S. independent-expenditure political committee created for the 2024 election cycle and associated with Elon Musk and Donald Trump-aligned electoral activity.

records.name: MAGA Inc.
records.definition: A U.S. independent-expenditure political committee supporting Donald Trump and aligned Republican candidates and causes.

records.name: Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)
records.definition: The CIA is a U.S. government intelligence agency established in 1947 that collects foreign intelligence, produces analysis and conducts covert action as directed by the president under applicable law.

records.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
records.type: U.S. federal law-enforcement and intelligence agency
records.definition: The FBI is the principal investigative arm of the U.S. Department of Justice and a member of the U.S. Intelligence Community, combining federal criminal investigation with domestic national-security intelligence responsibilities.
oversight: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court for applicable surveillance authorities

records.name: Mossad — Institute for Intelligence and Special Operations
records.definition: Mossad is Israel's foreign-intelligence and special-operations agency. Its public mission describes strategic intelligence collection, countering threats and clandestine operations in support of Israel's strategic objectives.
oversight: State Comptroller audit framework where applicable
